introHeading: Built for Staten Island's grand ballrooms and biggest nights
introParas: The 360 booth needs more overhead room than anything else we bring to Staten Island, and the island's grand ballrooms are exactly the kind of venue built for it. Guests step onto a lit platform, a camera arm sweeps a slow-motion circle around them, and a few seconds later they have a cinematic clip ready to share — which is why it's one of our most-booked booths for the island's biggest Sweet Sixteens and wedding receptions.

Ceiling height is the first thing we check. The camera arm needs 7.5ft of clearance minimum, and the larger banquet halls clustered near St. George and Great Kills generally clear that without a second thought — they're built for guest lists that fill the floor. Todt Hill and New Dorp venues run smaller and more residential, so if your event is in one of those neighborhoods, tell us the room and we'll confirm the fit before you book.

Setup takes about 20 minutes and we arrive a full hour early to test the arm before the room fills. Whether your venue is near the ferry in St. George or all the way south in Tottenville, Staten Island is within our standard service area — any bridge toll is built into your quote up front.

faqHeading: 360 Photo Booth on Staten Island — FAQ

faqs.q: Does a St. George banquet hall have enough ceiling height for the 360 arm?
faqs.a: Most do — the grand ballrooms clustered near St. George are generally built with the ceiling height and floor space this booth wants for a big Sweet Sixteen or wedding crowd. Send us the venue name and we will confirm before you book.

faqs.q: How much floor space does the 360 booth need at a Staten Island venue?
faqs.a: 8ft x 8ft minimum, 12ft x 12ft where the room allows it — a bigger footprint lets the crowd that gathers to watch stand comfortably instead of crowding the platform.

faqs.q: Is the 360 booth good for a Staten Island Sweet Sixteen?
faqs.a: It is one of our top picks for Sweet Sixteens specifically — the slow-motion video format is exactly what that guest list already shares, and the custom overlay can carry the honoree's name, colors or theme.

faqs.q: Can the 360 booth be set up in a smaller Todt Hill or New Dorp venue?
faqs.a: It can, though we'll want to see the room first — these run smaller and more residential than the island's grand ballrooms, so we confirm ceiling clearance and floor space before booking rather than assuming it fits.

faqs.q: Do you charge extra to bring the booth out to Staten Island?
faqs.a: No surprise fees beyond the standard bridge toll, which is already built into your quote. We confirm the number from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqs.q: What power does the booth need at a Staten Island venue?
faqs.a: A dedicated 15 or 20 amp outlet within reach of the platform. Older banquet halls sometimes run tighter circuits, so tell us about your venue's power and we will plan the placement around it.

faqs.q: Can the 360 booth be branded for a Staten Island corporate event?
faqs.a: Yes — the platform, overlay, intro and outro frames and sharing screen can all carry your logo and colors, useful for the corporate holiday parties and product launches we run at St. George's larger venues.

About 20 minutes once we're in the room. We build in a full hour ahead of your scheduled start so everything is tested before your first guest walks in. If you need us on site earlier than that, idle time is $150 per hour.

faqs.q: How do out-of-town guests reach a Staten Island venue?
faqs.a: The Staten Island Ferry runs free from Lower Manhattan to St. George, and from there it's a short car or taxi ride to most of the island. Guests driving from Brooklyn or New Jersey usually come across the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge. Tell us your venue and we can help guests figure out the easiest route for your invitations.
